# Summary


**Introduction**:
Volatile anaesthetics contribute to the environmental footprint of operating rooms.
The activated charcoal canister CONTRAfluran^TM^ (ZeoSys Medical GmbH, Luckenwalde, Germany)
passively captures sevoflurane at the anaesthesia machine exhaust port
for thermal desorption and pharmaceutical reuse.
The proportion of sevoflurane recaptured in clinical practice remains unclear.
The only study reporting a capture efficiency after desorption for sevoflurane found
markedly different values in its two operating rooms.
We therefore conducted the first multicentre study to identify the
real-world capture efficiency of the CONTRAfluran system.

**Methods**:
In this prospective observational study,
`r n_bottles_per_or` consecutive bottles of sevoflurane
were used in each participating operating room,
with a CONTRAfluran canister at the anaesthesia machine exhaust port.
Case characteristics were recorded for every anaesthesia case,
and used for nearest-neighbour selection of the
batch of `r n_agcs["final"]` canisters
required for desorption by ZeoSys.
Capture efficiency was defined as the mass of sevoflurane recovered
divided by the mass of sevoflurane attributable to these canisters.

**Results**:
From `r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[1L], "month"), "%B %Y")`
to `r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[2L], "month"), "%B %Y")`,
`r n_agcs["initial"]` canisters were used
in `r n_ors["initial"]` operating rooms across `r n_center["initial"]` hospitals
in Germany and Austria.
The `r n_agcs["final"]` analysed canisters were in place during
`r n_cases["final"]` anaesthesia cases, including
`r n_cases_inhalational` with inhalational anaesthesia.
Median fresh gas flow during inhalational anaesthesia was
`r fmt_num(flow_inhalational[2L])` l.min⁻¹
(interquartile range `r fmt_range(flow_inhalational[c(1L, 3L)])` l.min⁻¹).
ZeoSys recovered `r round(zeosys_sevo_weight_kg, 1)` kg of sevoflurane,
corresponding to a capture efficiency of `r round(recovery_pct_final, 1)`%.
The recovered sevoflurane accounted for `r round(zeosys_yield * 100, 0)`% of the canisters' weight gain.

**Discussion**:
The capture efficiency of `r round(recovery_pct_final, 1)`%
is lower than the 34% of our previous single-centre study
but within the range observed between its two operating rooms.
Under routine clinical conditions, canisters recovered approximately half
of the estimated theoretical maximum at minimal fresh gas flows.
Reducing sevoflurane use through minimal fresh gas flows
therefore remains the priority.
CONTRAfluran and other vapour capture technologies
can only recover part of what still leaves the breathing circuit.
